item.title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. A statement from the Editor, Mr Eze Anaba, said his death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession. Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism. Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager. Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career. The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family. At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. item.title: Inflation rate drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month. NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also declined to 19.13 percent from 19.59 percent in September. However, Month-on-Month, MoM, inflation rate rose by 0.43% in October, up by 0.38 percentage point from 0.06 percent recorded in September 2026. This increase also reflected in the MoM trend in food inflation for October. NBS stated: “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 percent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “Looking at the movement, the October 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9 percent compared to the October 2025 (18.97 percent) Headline inflation rate. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 percent, which was 0.38 percent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 percent). “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.” On food inflation, NBS, said: “The Food inflation rate in October 2026 was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis and stood at 16.3 per ent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “However, on a MoM basis, the Food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 percent , up by 0.80 percent points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent). “This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), green peas (Prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), etc” In October 2026, food inflation on a year-on-year basis was highest in Ondo (31.74 percent), Lagos (31.43 percent), and Imo (29.75 percent), while Nasarawa (3.7 percent), Bayelsa (7.11 percent) and Kano (7.13 percent) recorded the slowest rise in food inflation on a Year-on-Year basis. “On a MoM basis, however, October 2026 food inflation was highest in Yobe (18.41 percent), Kebbi (16.45 percent), and Borno (13.96 percent), while Lagos (-5.93 percent), Plateau (-5.83 percent), and Benue (-5.49 percent) recorded the slowest rise in Food inflation on a Month-on-Month basis.” Vanguard News The post Inflation rate drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kano govt, Kwankwasiyya Movement clash over attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy
item.description: *Alleged attack fictitiuos – Kano State govt *Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya blasts govt By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — Kano State government and the Kwankwasiyyah Movement were, yesterday, locked in a verbal war over alleged attack on the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in the state, weekend. NDC governorship candidate in Kano, Aminu Gwarzo, had alleged that during a campaign visit to Bichi on Sunday, the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of the party was attacked by thugs allegedly sent by the state government. The spokesperson for Gwarzo’s campaign, Ibrahim Shu’aibu, said the team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas without disruption before proceeding to Bichi where they were attcked. But reacting to the attack, yesterday, the Commissioner for Information in Kano State, Sanusi Tofa, dismissed the fact that there was an attack on the convoy of Kwankwaso in Bichi Local Government Area, describing the incident as fictitious. Tofa, who accused the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the reported attack in Bichi said: “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team has framed itself a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos.’’ Kano belongs to all, not those in power — Kwankwasiyya tells govt Replying the state government, the Kwankwasiyya Movement said Kano State belonged to all residents, regardless of their political affiliations. The movement said the government had a responsibility to protect everyone in the state and should not allow political differences to affect the safety and rights of citizens. In a statement by its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Mohammed, yesterday, the movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of making up the allegation to gain public sympathy. The statement specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident, rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the matter. It questioned why victims should be expected to provide evidence before the government could show concern over their safety. “Kano belongs to all its people, not exclusively to those occupying government offices. Its security, peace and democratic freedoms are collective responsibilities that must never be sacrificed on the altar of partisan politics,” the statement said. The movement argued that the responsibility for investigating allegations of criminal activities rested with security agencies, not the victims, accusing the commissioner of making premature conclusions without presenting the findings of any police investigation. The group called on Kano State police command to investigate the incident, establish what happened in Bichi and ensure that anyone found responsible was brought to justice. item.title: 2027: Opposition’s unity test
item.description: By Baba Martins, Daniel Adaji, Abuja; Sani Ibrahim Paki, Kano & Mumini AbdulKareem, Ilorin Talks among opposition political parties to pick a sole candidate to field in the coming presidential election are still on, with less than two months to the January 16, 2027 polls. Since August, opposition political parties have mooted dropping their individual platforms to rally around a common presidential candidate ahead of next year’s general elections, agreeing that it would be more daunting to enter the race on separate platforms. Presidential candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi; Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde; Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke and the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, have been involved in the talks. The G100, now known as the Coalition for Democracy, on which platform the idea was sold, has affirmed its commitment to sustaining the talks by making the parties forge a united political front. The coalition explained that deliberations on the matter would form the agenda of a summit of the opposition parties slated for November 23 in Abuja. A statement signed by the convener, Salihu Mohammed Lukman, on behalf of the coalition, said the physical presence of presidential candidates and their running mates at the meeting would demonstrate their willingness to work together in the national interest. “The Coalition attaches particular importance to the attendance, in person, of every presidential candidate and their running mates of the participating political parties,” he said. The coalition has held previous meetings for this purpose, which have yet to yield the expected results due to the inability of the major parties in the coalition to agree on a common candidate. Our correspondents found out that hope for a possible consensus rose since last week when some of the presidential candidates began to shift ground, saying they are not averse to stepping down if a credible candidate is picked from among them. Duke had stated last week that he was ready to step down for any candidate decided by the coalition. “But at the end of the day, I’ll be sportsmanlike about it. If the group, and so far there are quite a number of us, comes up with an agreement that this is the best person to lead the coalition, you can’t say you’re a democrat and not be subject to the rules of democracy,” he stated recently. Our correspondents report that the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, has confirmed that major opposition presidential candidates are actively discussing a possible alliance ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde disclosed that he is currently engaged in discussions with Atiku and Obi, as opposition politicians explore possible ways of working together ahead of the polls. item.title: ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo LAGOS—Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr. Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes, if elected governor, saying his administration will use increased Federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and welfare of residents. Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.” The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy. Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.” He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS. item.title: Abia approves ₦1.04bn for SMEs, reviews ASEPA workers’ pay
item.description: …₦382.9m disbursed to 31 businesses By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has secured approval for ₦1.041 billion in intervention funding for small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), in a move aimed at expanding businesses, stimulating job creation and improving access to affordable credit. Of the amount, ₦382.9 million has already been disbursed to 29 micro-enterprises and two small and medium-scale businesses, while another ₦206.7 million in approved applications is undergoing documentation ahead of disbursement. The state government also announced a review of the remuneration of ad-hoc workers engaged by the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA), with the new payment structure taking effect from November 2026. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, who disclosed the developments during the weekly briefing on the State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia, said the SME intervention was being implemented through the Bank of Industry (BOI). Kanu, represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Fredinald Ekeoma, said the initiative was part of Governor Alex Otti’s administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s productive sector and create sustainable employment opportunities. Providing further details, Commissioner for Industries and SMEs, Mazi Mike Akpara, said the outstanding approved facilities would be released once beneficiaries fulfilled the necessary conditions, including documentation and provision of guarantors and collateral, where applicable. He stressed that access to the intervention was not restricted by political affiliation, insisting that any genuine business operating in Abia was eligible. “Whether you belong to the Labour Party, PDP or APC, we are not concerned about that. Once you are doing business in Abia and can provide evidence of your business operations, you are eligible to benefit. “SMEs are the engine of the economy, and this initiative is intended to encourage and strengthen them,” Akpara said. He said interested businesses could access the programme through the Ministry of Industries and SMEs at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Secretariat, Umuahia, or the BOI office in Aba. Akpara described the facility as a major relief for local entrepreneurs, given its relatively low interest rates of 8.5 per cent for overdrafts and 7.5 per cent for other facilities, with a three-year repayment period. He contrasted the rates with commercial bank lending rates, which he said could rise to between 28 and 30 per cent, arguing that the intervention would ease the financing burden on businesses and improve their capacity to expand. In another development, Kanu said the Ministry of Industries and SMEs had verified and documented more than 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya-Umuogo-Nsukwe Industrial Cluster. item.title: Dry season farming: Shettima directs swift release of 3m fertiliser bags nationwide
item.description: ‎—Orders ONSA to monitor declared stocks ahead of distribution ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President Senator Kashim Shettima has directed relevant government agencies and stakeholders in the fertiliser industry to expedite arrangements for the production and release of over three million bags of fertiliser to farmers across the country ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming. ‎ ‎The directive followed President Bola Tinubu’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, aimed at making fertiliser more affordable, boosting food production and reviving Nigeria’s fertiliser blending industry. ‎ ‎The Vice President gave the directive on Monday at the Presidential Villa during a meeting with stakeholders in the fertiliser sector in Abuja, where the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) disclosed that available raw materials could support the production of approximately three million bags of NPK fertiliser within the next few weeks. ‎ ‎He also directed the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to verify and track fertiliser stocks declared by stakeholders to ensure transparency, accountability and a hitch-free distribution exercise. ‎ ‎He further urged the NSA’s office to ensure that farming communities in states facing security challenges are not neglected in the distribution programme, stressing the need for the intervention to reach farmers in vulnerable and hard-to-access areas. ‎ ‎Speaking on the broader economic importance of the presidential intervention, the Vice President said revitalising Nigeria’s fertiliser industry would strengthen agricultural productivity while creating jobs and supporting rural livelihoods. ‎ ‎”A strong fertilizer value chain supports hundreds of thousands of direct and indirect jobs. Revitalizing this sector is therefore important not only for agriculture but also for employment, rural livelihoods and economic activities across the country,” he stated. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima expressed concern that many of the country’s fertiliser blending plants were operating below capacity despite the growing demand for affordable agricultural inputs. ‎ ‎”Today, many of our fertilizer blending plants are operating below capacity at the same time the high cost of fertilizer continues to increase the cost of production for our farmers,” he observed. ‎ ‎According to him, President Tinubu’s intervention is designed to address these challenges by stimulating domestic production, restoring jobs and making fertiliser available to farmers at affordable prices. ‎ ‎”The government wants to support the rehabilitation and full utilization of our fertilizer blending capacity. item.title: Wike to opposition: Stop creating chaos to blame Tinubu
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, yesterday, accused opposition political parties of deliberately fomenting trouble to make it appear that President Bola Tinubu is responsible for political violence ahead of the 2027 elections. Wike made the allegation during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) in the FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja. The minister, who expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in the upcoming elections, claimed that opposition parties knew they had already lost and were creating political tension to discredit the ruling party. Wike said: “You have what it takes to win this election. The other parties know. Let me just tell you the simple truth. The other parties know they have lost the election. “What are they doing now? What they are doing now is to foment crisis—foment problems to make it look as if it is the government; it is the presidential candidate of the APC party who is fomenting trouble. “They (opposition) are the ones causing trouble. You (APC PCC) don’t need to cause trouble because you have already won the election. “They (opposition parties) foment trouble and report as if they are not the ones that have created that problem. So, we must be on alert.” Wike also told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general elections. He warned the members against assuming the contest was already won, saying the election was a chance for the APC to show its political strength in the territory. On how to sell the president’s record, he said: “You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign.” Wike also dared opposition politicians to set projects built before 2023 beside those delivered since Tinubu took office, arguing that the work going on in the city centre and the satellite towns spoke for itself. item.title: 2027: APC rallies deepening Nigerians’ anger, Kawu warns party leaders
item.description: …Senator decries disconnect between northern masses and political elite, urges grassroots mobilisation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Petroleum (Downstream), Senator Kawu Sumaila Suleiman (APC, Kano South), has warned the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) that displays of opulence, celebrations and merrymaking at presidential campaign rallies are deepening the pains and anger of Nigerians. The senator, who is the APC senatorial candidate for the January 16, 2027 election, said there was a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between ordinary people in the North and the political elite. In a statement addressed to party leaders and members on Monday, his second intervention on the matter, Suleiman called for a change in the party’s approach and strategy ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged the APC leadership and Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) to prioritise effective communication of President Bola Tinubu’s policies and ongoing reforms to Nigerians at the grassroots. The lawmaker also called on the party to identify and empower credible individuals and stakeholders with genuine grassroots influence in their respective constituencies rather than relying on what he described as “Abuja politicians” and entitled individuals disconnected from the people. In the statement titled, “A Clarion Call for Self-Reflection, Humility, and Grassroots Reconnection”, Suleiman said the party’s message was still not reaching ordinary Nigerians. He said: “Following my earlier message, we must once again be completely honest with ourselves: our message is still not reaching the grassroots. We need to acknowledge and accept that there is a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between the common people in the North and the political elites. We must change our approach and strategy. “There is an urgent need to effectively communicate our government’s policies and the ongoing reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directly to the grassroots.” The senator warned that the celebratory atmosphere at campaign rallies was insensitive to the hardship and insecurity confronting many Nigerians, particularly in the North. He urged party leaders to remember victims of terrorism, thousands of Nigerians displaced from their communities and those forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic. “The current displays of celebration, opulence, and pomp-dancing and merrymaking during presidential campaign rallies are only deepening the pains and anger of the citizens. “We must remember the countless people currently trapped in the hands of terrorists, the thousands suffering in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps, and those who have been forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic,” he said. item.title: Don’t turn churches into campaign arena, Soludo cautions politicians
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State, on Sunday, cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into a political arena, stating that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of all political persuasions. Soludo made the remark during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor stressed the need for the men of God to clearly separate politics from worship. According to Soludo, the place of worship should be a holy place where people of all political persuasion should come and worship God in peace. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. He recalled that six months before his election, he took a deliberate decision never to go to any church to cup a microphone to ask them to vote for him or to campaign. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the government house chapel until the election day and afterwards,” the governor stated. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message, and it is my kind of consistency of character”, he further said. item.title: Obi, Kwankwaso have God’s grace to dislodge Tinubu — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A chieftain of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Babachir Lawal, has said Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso, his running mate, have God’s backing to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, who made the declaration during an appearance on Arise Television late Sunday, cited the “widespread support” Obi and Kwankwaso enjoyed as a pointer to God’s grace upon their lives. He said: “I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them. “The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.” He said his experience in politics had enabled him to recognise signs that could favour the opposition alliance, adding that he previously occupied a similar position during the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries. “So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes,’’ he said. Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. , saying the party had established structures and systems to achieve its objective. “We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government. “We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 per cent confident,’’ he said. Lawal added that the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to convert the popularity of its presidential candidates into electoral success by ensuring that votes were protected and counted. “This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said. Lawal dismissed concerns over recent departure of Yunusa Tanko, former national coordinator of the Obidient Movement; Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe, and the former NDC’s deputy national publicity secretary, from Obi’s camp, saying politicians were free to leave parties when their expectations were not met. He compared the development with the exit of some politicians from Tinubu’s inner circle, including Kashim Imam and Rauf Aregbesola. “I was with Bola Tinubu, but I left. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu. But he has left. These are big politicians. But they left Bola Tinubu. “Leaving a political party is only natural. Nigeria is like a big company with many political parties. And people come in there with their own different ideas about what they can get out of it

item.title: Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles
item.description: …SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy .. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months. Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period. The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion. Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. item.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
item.description: …Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year. Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state. The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos. In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy. He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state. “This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said. He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities. “It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added. Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state. item.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu. The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital. Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo. “My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said. According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs. He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.” Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism. He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician. “Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said. The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions. He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed. Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA. item.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
item.description: … Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society By Ogochukwu Agha lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others. The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million. Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness. “The essence of life is what you can give to others.” Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?” She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities. The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges. Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years. She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education. “YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said. The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support. The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions. item.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added. item.title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots. The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector. He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system. The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential. He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay. Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time. He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians. He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting. Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20. She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate. According to her, the Technical Committee would review proceedings and the implementation status of resolutions reached at the 66th Regular National Council on Health, consider memoranda submitted by the Federal Government, state governments and other ministries, and develop recommendations for consideration by the Council. He said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, who was of the Labour Party (LP) in 2023, won in Lagos due to the support received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS group, youths, and workers. ﻿ He, however, said Obi would not win in Lagos in the forthcoming presidential election. item.title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition. “Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said. FILES: Segun Sowunmi on Channels Television’s Politics Today “If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked. North Presidency Calculations The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark. The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress for the 2027 general elections. The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed. Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain. “As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said. He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”. “Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added. item.title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
item.description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic. “I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said. Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. “I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.
